Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:60: To understand the difference between "cleaving," "yearning," and "desiring" - if the matter were merely repeated in different words, this would not indicate the affection; rather, we must say that each of these terms indicates an aspect of affection that the other does not indicate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:61: "Cleaving" indicates a person's cleaving of his soul to the soul of his fellow, along the lines of (I Kings 1:12) "in whom Solomon clings for love," and likewise (Ruth 1:14) "but Ruth clung to her" - meaning the cleaving of her will to her. Nevertheless, this cleaving does not indicate unity to such a great degree, for it is still possible that the cleaving one separate, and the proof is from the very place our Sages, of blessed memory, learned "cleaving" from: "as the loincloth clings to the loins of a man, so have I made cling to Me all the house of Israel," etc., as explained above - and a loincloth is sometimes clinging to a person and sometimes not clinging, when he unties it from himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:62: The word "chashak" [yearning], however, indicates a stronger bond of love, for we find that the Torah uses this word for the matter of bonding and union - (Exodus 38:12) "and their fillets of silver" [chishukeihem kesef] - meaning tightened and bonded, for the pillars had silver wires that were tightened and bonded and bound around them, as is done with wooden barrels to tighten them - so the Radak explains under the root "chashak."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:63: "Chafetz" [desire] is even more - that a person's whole will and entire intent be turned toward her face, not moving away from her even for one hour, along the lines of what is said (I Chronicles 28:9) "with a whole heart and a willing soul"; and this is (Genesis 34:19) "and the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he desired Jacob's daughter" - he did not delay the matter, and it was as though he were dying with love for her, having no other will in the world but this alone. Likewise, the reality of union in Scripture is termed with the word "chefetz," as in (I Kings 10:13) "all her desire that she asked," concerning the Queen of Sheba, which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain to mean that he came upon her. It is further explained in the Zohar (Yitro 89a), on the verse (Isaiah 56:4) "and choose what I desire" - "what I desire" unqualified refers to the union of the Matronita - the reason being that in union, all of a person's will and heart and all his limbs are turned toward one face.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:64: Therefore, from the proofs brought in the passage for "cleaving" and "yearning," we learn that "yearning" is understood to be more than "cleaving," and "desiring" more than "yearning." "Cleaving" is brought from the verse "but you who cleave"; you already know what I explained above, that this does not indicate the Holy One, blessed be He's cleaving to them so much as their cleaving to Him. The second verse indicates greater affection: (Deuteronomy 7:7) "not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did the Lord yearn for you" - it appears that He of Himself yearned for them without any prior arousal of deed on their part; but it does not indicate affection to as great a degree, since our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Chullin 89a): "not because you were more numerous" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, "I yearn for you," etc. - because the Holy One, blessed be He, gives you greatness, yet you diminish yourselves. The third verse (Malachi 3:12) "and they shall call you happy," applies to the future to come - "for you shall be a delightsome land" - it appears that this is a level not yet attained, but rather, "you shall be a delightsome land" - and the interpretation of "chefetz" is desire/will - that His will, blessed be He, in us is without any cause at all, but rather His desire and will in them is from great affection, like a person who desires this land more than that, even though they are equal.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:65: Along the way we have explained, that these totals correspond to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, the matter is settled - that each word indicates in the matter of affection and love something the other does not indicate, and as we explained above, that the aspect of the love of the nefesh is not equal to the love of the ruach, nor the love of the ruach to the love of the neshamah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:66: It remains for us to explain a matter in the passage very relevant to the matter of love, namely to know why the author of the passage needed to derive all three from the passage concerning that wicked man; and we saw that this is a lengthy matter, so we shall explain it in a separate chapter, to give the reader some breathing room.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:1: This chapter will explain the love of the Shechinah, and how our love for her should be so that it cannot be separated. This is the reality learned from the passage concerning that wicked man, and its explanation is based on what the commentators explain, particularly Rabbi Menachem Recanati, peace be upon him, who writes that Shechem son of Chamor the Hivite, who came upon Dinah, is a secret allusion to the serpent that came upon Eve - "Hivi" being related to the language of "serpent" [chivya] - and Dinah, as is already known, the Zohar explains, is the judgment of the kingdom, judgment [dina demalchuta dina] - for Leah, the supernal mother, bore six sons and one daughter, and this daughter is the Shechinah, who is judgment, as is known. Since that wicked man, on account of sin, had his soul cleave to Dinah, daughter of Jacob, in cleaving, in yearning, in desiring, so a person's soul should fittingly cleave to the Shechinah in these three realities, as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:2: This was also the intent of the author of the passage in bringing the three expressions of affection with which the Holy One, blessed be He, showed His love for Israel - to show us that just as He desires so greatly to cleave to us, so it is fitting that we cleave to Him in these three aspects. Concerning this the Torah commanded, saying (Leviticus 19:18) "and you shall love your fellow [rea] as yourself," and our Sages, of blessed memory, already explain (Shemot Rabbah 27:1; Zohar Beshalach 55b) that your "fellow" [rea] is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Proverbs 27:10) "do not forsake your friend and your father's friend." And further, the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His great love for us, calls us "friends," as it is said (Psalms 122:8) "for the sake of my brothers and my friends," and likewise (ibid. 148:14) "for the children of Israel, a people near to Him"; therefore it says "and you shall love your friend as yourself" - your friend, who is the Holy One, blessed be He; "as yourself" - with the love you wish for yourself, just as if you have a friend, you want him to love you, so the Holy One, blessed be He, who is your friend, wants you to love Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:3: Further, "as yourself" may mean: it is known to us that if two friends love each other, and one of them, out of his great love for his friend, does good to him, clothing him, feeding him, giving him drink, and other good things, it is fitting that his friend not be ungrateful, but love him as his own soul; and if it happens that the friend who did good to him should need something, it is fitting that the one who already received from his friend repay that goodness according to his ability, and if he lacks the ability, he should at least show his good heart toward him and that he has nothing with which to repay his debt to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:4: So too is the matter concerning the moral: the Holy One, blessed be He, preceded [us] with His goodness to every creature, and especially to His people Israel, with several miracles and wonders He did and does with us, as we shall discuss below, with the Lord's help. Therefore it is fitting that a person recognize the goodness of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is his friend, and love Him, so as not to be ungrateful, etc., as is explained in the Tikkunim several times (see 37a), and he must do an act of kindness with Him and with His Shechinah through the deed of Torah and mitzvot, for (Proverbs 27:8) "as a bird that wanders from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place." Concerning the matter of acts of kindness, we shall quote Rashbi's, peace be upon him, words below. And at all times the reality of love should not be lacking, for (Deuteronomy 10:12) "what does the Lord ask of you but to fear and to love," for fear and love are in the heart and soul, matters within your own body that you need not seek from another - this is "from you" [me'imcha, in the Hebrew of that verse]; and so it says elsewhere (ibid. 30:14) "for the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:5: According to this interpretation, "your friend" applies both to the righteous man and to the Shechinah. We find support for this from the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Terumah 169b), concerning the sixth of the seven blessings recited for bridegroom and bride, "grant abundant joy to these loving friends" - our Sages, of blessed memory, say, "Tzaddik and Tzedek [Yesod and Malchut] are 'friends' and 'loving,' for they never depart one from another" - so far. Since we find that both together are called "friends," it implies that each one individually is called "your friend" unqualified, and this is not strange, since we already find in the Talmud that the female is called "your friend" - our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Kiddushin 41a): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, it is forbidden for a man to betroth a woman until he sees her, lest he see something unseemly in her and come to hate her, and the Merciful One says (Leviticus 19:18) "and you shall love your friend as yourself" - so far. Here we see that the female too is included in "and you shall love your friend."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:6: Concerning "and you shall love your friend" applied to the righteous, it may be explained in another way, along the lines of what is explained in Rashbi's words (Zohar, Vayechi 216a), concerning "the righteous shall inherit the land," see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:7: Concerning "your friend" applied to the Shechinah, it may also be explained in another way, based on what was explained above in chapter 3, from the Zohar (Bereishit 51a), concerning "but you who cleave to the Lord your God" - that Israel cleave to that blue-black fire; we find that they are the wick to which the fire clings, and just as that fire needs oil to burn, and if not, it goes out, so this holy fire that rests upon our heads - (Deuteronomy 4:24) "for the Lord your God is a consuming fire" - its consumption is Torah and prayer and mitzvot, and this is the oil provided - this is (Ecclesiastes 9:8) "let your garments always be white, and let oil not be lacking on your head." This is likewise explained in Rashbi's words, of blessed memory (Zohar, portion of Balak 187a): he opened and said, (Ecclesiastes 2:14) "the wise man's eyes are in his head," etc. - and is there any other place for a person's eyes than his head? Or perhaps in his body or in his arm, which "produces" the wise man more than all the world's inhabitants? Rather, the verse is certainly so: we learn, a person should not walk four cubits with his head uncovered - why? Because the Shechinah rests upon his head; and all who are wise, their eyes and words are upon their head, upon the One who rests and stands upon his head. And when his eyes are there, to know that this light kindled upon his head requires oil, since a person's body is the wick and the light is kindled above, Solomon the king cried out and said, "and let oil not be lacking on your head" - "on your head," since the light on his head requires oil, and these are good deeds; and therefore "the wise man's eyes are in his head" and not elsewhere - so far. And in the Tikkunim (60b), it says that Israel are the wick, the Torah is the oil, the Shechinah is the flame - this is [the meaning of] (Job 29:3) "when His candle shone above my head" - so far. Along these lines, the verse "and let oil not be lacking on your head" means that he should provide oil, which is Torah, to the candle upon his head.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:8: With this we understand the verse (Isaiah 62:6) "you who remind the Lord, take no rest for yourselves" - because their arousal depends on the lower beings, as is explained in the Song of Songs and in several places. My teacher, peace be upon him, explains that this is what David meant (Psalms 30:13) "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever" - "glory" being the Shechinah, and in order for her to sing above and not be silent, I too need to be below, so that I may forever give You thanks.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:9: With this we understand "and you shall love your friend as yourself" - meaning, you shall love the Shechinah, to give her constant arousal of deeds so that she never lack, just as you desire for yourself; for it is known that she is the Mother who bestows upon the lower beings the flow of life and good, and just as you desire and love that life and flow never be lacking to you for a moment, so you should love to provide oil above, as I explained, since the upper beings need the lower beings - this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, say: "the Shechinah's presence among the lower beings is a need of the Above," as my teacher, peace be upon him, explains this matter at length in Sefer Pardes Rimonim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:10: Along these lines, concerning the reality of cleaving, yearning, and desiring, we must love the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, in all three, just as we desire that the Holy One, blessed be He, love us in all three, since there is no complete love except in all three - this is a fourth interpretation concerning "and you shall love your friend as yourself."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:11: Let us return to the discourse to understand the passage, which we said, that the author of the passage bringing all three, teaching us from the passage concerning that wicked man, is to teach us that a person is obligated to love the Shechinah with all three, and the reason is that it is impossible for the Shechinah to be unified above unless the righteous man first performs these three aspects with her, and then, through these three, the Shechinah makes a covenant with him, since through him she is made a vessel, as we shall explain - and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Sanhedrin 22b): a woman makes a covenant only with one who has made her a vessel [i.e., through consummation].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:12: The first, "cleaving," as it is said (Genesis 34:3) "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" - the reality of cleaving is that a person cleave his soul and direct his whole intent toward unifying the Shechinah and separating from her all the kelipot, and likewise to separate from his own thought all foreign thoughts, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Vayelech 285a), that at the time of union one must unify the Shechinah in thought without any admixture of chaff and straw - and we quoted this passage in the last chapter of the Gate of Fear - and this is "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" - meaning, to this one, who is Dinah, he cleaves, and to no other at all; and just as it is true, what our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Nedarim 20b), "let him not drink from this cup and set his eye on another cup" - and this is called "a son of substitution" - and how strict Rashbi was about this (Zohar, Vayetze 155a, in Tikkunei Zohar) - along these lines, one must also not have his intent turn toward the Shechinah while thinking in the filth of his thoughts, which are external, for then he is found to be separating, God forbid; rather, he must cleave to the Shechinah properly and separate everything else from her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:13: Further, one who loves two women, his love for them is not complete, since they are rivals to each other; and in order for a woman's love for her husband to be firmly and beautifully fixed, it is when she sees that he loves no other woman in the world but her alone - then she will make a covenant of complete love with him. So too the Shechinah will not bind her love to a person who loves worldly matters, and therefore the essence of love is that a person love nothing in the world more than his love for Him, blessed be He, and his love for Him, blessed be He, should exceed his love for his wife and children and other worldly matters. For what causes a person to be separated from love of the Holy One, blessed be He, at the time he stands in prayer or is engaged in Torah, so that evil, foreign thoughts come to him, is because he is not firmly fixed in love of the Holy One, blessed be He, exceeding love of the matters of this world; he loves both this and that, and would that he not love the matters of this world more than love of the Holy One, blessed be He - but since the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that his love for Him is not as it should be, and the person abandons Him, the Holy One, blessed be He, is likewise abandoned and separates from him, along the lines of the verse (I Chronicles 28:9) "if you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever" - and then evil thought rules over him. Therefore one must separate the love of this world, which is the love of strangers and the love of raisin cakes (Hosea 3:1), for all these are external, and cleave his heart to holy love, like Dinah, daughter of Jacob.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:14: Now, with what I have explained, one doubt concerning this matter is resolved: most verses in the Torah indicate "and to Him you shall cleave" - meaning, to Him, who is the Tree of Life, you shall cleave - yet here we say it is a mitzvah to cleave to her [the Shechinah]. Rather, the matter is that this cleaving serves only to exclude one's cleaving to another, along the lines of what is said, "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" and not another, as we explained the intent, to separate the external and everything else.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:15: Further, at the beginning of entry [into service], cleaving to her is necessarily required, along the lines of (Leviticus 16:2) "with this [bezot] shall Aaron come into the sanctuary," which is explained in the Tikkunim (21b), and it is explained there that whoever performs a mitzvah, or prays, or engages in Torah, must first direct his whole intent toward the Shechinah, to unify her; therefore Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Tikkunim 33b): come and see, if a person raises in his thought, in his prayer, [the intent] toward the Shechinah, or in each and every mitzvah he performs, immediately, when he knocks at the gate of the King's palace - a prophet, a seer, a sage, or a righteous man - the moment he calls at the gate, if the Shechinah has ascended there, YHVH will answer immediately, and will not wait for a servant or appointee to open, but rather He Himself opens it for him, out of the affection and love He has for him, like a groom toward his bride; and if the Shechinah has not ascended in that prayer or mitzvah, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not consider it worthy to open His palace for him, even through a messenger, and he is not worthy to enter the King's palace, and of him it is said "outside you shall stand" - and from outside they take his requests through a messenger or appointee; and if his prayer did not ascend properly, they push him outside and lock the gates before him, and of them it is said (Proverbs 1:28) "then they shall call me but I will not answer, they shall seek me early but shall not find me." And so, when each of Israel calls to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the Shema or in prayer or in any mitzvah, if the Shechinah is not there, He does not descend there - this is [the meaning of] (Exodus 20:21) "in every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you," and Onkelos translates, "in every place I cause My Shechinah to dwell there," etc. - for when a person raises the Shechinah through his mitzvot to the Holy One, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, descends upon him because of her. And therefore the prophet says (Jeremiah 9:23) "let him not glory," etc., "but let him who glories glory in this" - and this has already been established - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:16: Here it is explained, in the passage, that the Holy One, blessed be He, truly opens it for him out of the affection and love He has for her, and therefore a person must direct his whole intent to unifying the Shechinah, and in this respect is cleaving to her - this is "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" and "and he loved the girl" and "he spoke to the girl's heart" - all these are preparations for union. And the wicked man reversed the order, lying with her and afflicting her and only afterward "his soul cleaved" - and this is not the proper order; rather, first "his soul cleaved to Dinah," meaning to this one and not another, and afterward that he cleave to her in love, and speak to her comforting words, and afterward yearning, and afterward desire, as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:17: Further, there is another matter in "cleaving," found in the story of Ruth, that Boaz said to her (Ruth 2:8) "have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass from here, but cleave here to my maidens" - this indicates two aspects: the first, "turn away from evil," namely "do not glean in another field," since "other" unqualified is Samael, "other gods." The second, "and cleave here to my maidens."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:18: This is likewise explained by our Sages, of blessed memory, in the Pesikta - their words: "'do not go to glean in another field' - alludes to 'you shall have no other gods.' 'And also do not pass from here' - alludes to (Exodus 20:2) 'this is my God, and I will glorify Him.' 'And cleave here' - (Deuteronomy 4:4) 'but you who cleave.' 'To my maidens' - these are the righteous, who are called 'maidens' [na'arot, related to na'ar, youth], as it is said (Job 40:29) 'will you play with him as with a bird, or will you bind him for your maidens?'" - so far. This explicitly teaches all the exposition - it teaches two aspects concerning cleaving: one, "but you who cleave," according to its plain sense, as known; the second, that in order to cleave to her, one must cleave to the righteous, as our Sages, of blessed memory, expound (see Bemidbar Rabbah 22:1) on "and to Him you shall cleave" - is it possible to cleave to the Shechinah? Is it not already said (Deuteronomy 4:24) "for the Lord your God is a consuming fire"? Rather, one should cleave to the righteous.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:19: It may be said, along the lines of the Zohar, that "maidens" unqualified refers to the seven maidens explained several times (Zohar, Pekudei 260b), for what is said, "and cleave here to my maidens," refers to the cleaving of the attribute Kaf-Heh to the seven maidens fit to be given to her from the King's house, which are the seven Holy Palaces that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the portion of Pekudei (244b), where it is explained how the Palaces are repaired in the order of prayer for the repair of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:20: Along these lines, "and he spoke to her heart" refers to the blessings of the Shema, which are her adornments, particularly in the blessing of love [Ahavah Rabbah], which ascends into the Palace of Love, and there we arouse, through this blessing, appeasement and reconciliation with the Holy One, blessed be He, that He come to unite with her - as is explained in the Tikkunim (45a): "woe to human beings whose hearts and eyes are sealed, who do not strive to know the honor of their Master, to appease Him with His Shechinah through several supplications and reconciliations, to bring Him down to the Shechinah - how much more so to arouse in Him love toward her, as they instituted 'who chooses His people Israel with love'" - so far. The meaning is that "His people Israel" are the souls of Israel comprised within her, since she is called Knesset Yisrael, and the Holy One, blessed be He, chooses her and them with love, since it is the way of the husband to love his wife, the wife of his youth, as it is said (Isaiah 54:6) "and a wife of youth, though she be despised."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:21: Above this matter, they explain that in the Shema Yisrael we call to Israel, meaning Tiferet, and he comes to unite with her - their words (Tikkunim 45a): another interpretation: (Exodus 32:18) "it is the sound of song I hear" - this is the afflicted crying of "Anochi" [I], which cries out every day to her husband, she and her children, and they call to him twice, evening and morning, "Shema Yisrael"; and every person who has affliction from the Shechinah, who is afflicted in exile, far from her husband, calls to Him every day, "Shema Yisrael," that He should descend to her - certainly of him it is said, "it is the sound of affliction I hear" - the sound of that afflicted one, I hear - so far. Behold, all this is comfort and speaking to her heart, by which she is somewhat comforted from the exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:22: Just as the incident of Shechem with Dinah occurred at a time of exile when the moon was not in its proper repair, as explained in the Song of Songs, until Moses came; and further, our father Jacob, peace be upon him, was outside his home - had he been in the place of his fathers, in Be'er Sheva, this incident would not have happened to him - and that wicked man did these three things to her, as explained in the passage - so now, while the Shechinah is in exile, a person must repair the Shechinah and appease her with these repairs: in cleaving, as we explained, in love, in speaking to her heart. We shall further elaborate below on the matter of her repairs and speaking to her heart in other aspects. And concerning cleaving in the seven maidens, there is another aspect that will be explained in the matter of Torah and prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:23: "Yearning" has two aspects, along the way we explained for "cleaving": the first, that after one's soul cleaves to the Shechinah in every single mitzvah he performs, he must do it with yearning and the enflaming of the heart in very great love, and this is the matter of "the desire of the heart" [re'uta delibba] explained in the Zohar several times (Yitro 93b); and it is impossible for the desire of the heart, which is this yearning, unless thought of the Name, blessed be He, and love of Him precede it, and from love this yearning is born.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:24: This matter of yearning, which is the desire of the heart, is explained in the words of Rashbi, of blessed memory (Zohar, Shemot 198b): "take from among yourselves an offering for the Lord; let everyone whose heart makes him willing bring it" (Exodus 35:5) - come and see, at the time a person sets his desire toward the service of his Master, that desire first ascends upon the heart, which is the foundation and root of the whole body, and afterward that good desire ascends upon the limbs of the body, and the desire of all the limbs of the body and the desire of the heart join together as one, and they draw upon themselves the radiance of the Shechinah to dwell with them, and that person becomes a portion of the Holy One, blessed be He - this is [the meaning of] "take from among yourselves an offering" - "from among yourselves" was the drawing to receive upon yourselves that offering, to become a portion for the Lord. And if you say that this matter is not within a person's power - come and see what is written, "let everyone whose heart makes him willing bring the Lord's offering" - "everyone whose heart makes him willing," certainly - whoever's heart is willing draws the Shechinah toward himself - this is [the meaning of] "bring it" - although she is in a state of ascent above, "bring it" from the supernal place, to draw her to dwell with him" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:25: Along these lines, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain, concerning the workings of the inclination in man, in beraitot found in Tractate Kallah (chapter 2), in manuscript - their words: we learn, a person's inclination overpowers him every day, as it is said (Genesis 6:5) "and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" - from this our Sages expounded: improper thought leads to desire, desire leads to love, love leads to pursuit, pursuit leads to deed - to teach you how hard it is to turn back from one to the other; and correspondingly, in repentance: abstinence leads to watchfulness, watchfulness leads to alacrity, etc. - so far, their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:26: For our purpose, concerning love: improper thought and desire are "cleaving," and love and pursuit are "yearning," which is the desire of the heart. Here we shall quote Rashbi's, peace be upon him, words below regarding the desire of the heart, to pursue - and "deed" is "desire" [chefetz], for the deed is the ultimate goal of the sought-after desire; and we find that pursuit comes only from desire and love, and this is what he explained, that from love this yearning is born.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:27: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Terumah 128a) that the way a person acquires the Shechinah to rest upon him is essentially the desire of the heart. He says there that the kelipot rest upon a person gratuitously, enticing him to perform a deed so that they come to dwell with him; and he says afterward: but the holy spirit is not so, only with complete reward and great and abundant striving and self-preparation and purification of one's dwelling, and with the desire of his heart and soul; and would that he could bring it about that He make His dwelling with him! And with all this, a person must walk in a straight path, not turning right or left, and if not, he immediately withdraws and distances Himself from him, and he cannot bring it about as before. And therefore it is written "and they shall take for Me an offering from every man" - from him who is called a "man" [ish], who has overcome his inclination, for whoever overcomes his inclination is called a "man." "Whose heart makes him willing" - what is "whose heart makes him willing"? Rather, that his heart desires the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 27:8) "to You my heart says," "the rock of my heart" (ibid. 73:26), and "a good heart" (Proverbs 15:15), and "and his heart was merry" (Ruth 3:7) - all of these are said concerning the Holy One, blessed be He. Here too, "whose heart makes him willing" - from him you shall take My offering, since it is found there and nowhere else.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:28: How do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires him and makes His dwelling with him? When we see that that person's desire is together, with the desire of his heart, to pursue and strive after Him with his heart, his soul, and his desire - certainly we know there the Shechinah rests upon him; then we need to acquire that person for complete payment - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:29: Here it is explained, at the end of the passage, that the essence of everything is the desire of the heart, and this is the explanation of "whose heart makes him willing"; and it explains that this desire of the heart is the yearning of the heart. And he says, "with the desire of the heart, to pursue and strive after Him with his heart, his soul, and his desire" - it appears that he should strive to pursue the Holy One, blessed be He, and His commandments, and to cleave to Him with heart and soul and the desire of the heart, which is the enflaming of the heart we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:30: The preceding preparations he mentions - "with complete reward," and "with great and abundant striving" - are all preparations for cleaving. And all this the verse comprises in saying "from every man," as we said, that a "man" is one who overcomes his inclination, and the preparations needed to overcome one's inclination are those mentioned at the beginning of the passage, and they are what cause cleaving, as I explained above, that it is impossible to cleave unless one separates the kelipot from himself, which is the subduing of the inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:31: The interpretation of "with complete reward" may allude to the matter of "acquire for yourself a companion" (Avot 1:6) - meaning, acquire at a price. "With great and abundant striving" refers to the matter of "alacrity leads to the holy spirit," as we elaborated in explaining the passage (Avodah Zarah 20b), "Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says, watchfulness leads to alacrity." "Self-preparation" refers to preparing oneself, along the lines of "prepare to meet your God" (Amos 4:12), which is explained in the portion of Noach (Zohar 72a), and we quoted its words in the Gate of Holiness. "Purification of his dwelling" - "and your camp shall be holy" (Deuteronomy 23:15). "And with the desire of his heart" - this is the yearning of the heart. "That he walk in a straight path" - as Solomon the king, peace be upon him, says (Proverbs 4:27) "do not turn to the right or the left" - the interpretation of "do not turn to the right" is the intent expressed in (Ecclesiastes 7:16) "do not be overly righteous"; and "the left" - do not be overly wicked; meaning, from the extremes, take the middle. And he says that one who is called "a man who overcomes his inclination" refers to the subduing of all matters of the material, the reason being that it is impossible for the light of the Shechinah to cleave to one who is physical, sharing in matters of the material, since the inclination will draw him toward matters of the material; rather, [it cleaves] to one in whom the good inclination rules over his evil inclination, since the good inclination, from the side of the Shechinah, flows as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, and he is found to be completely righteous, and therefore it is fitting that the Shechinah bind herself to him. And the yearning is "his heart makes him willing," the desire of the heart, as I explained, meaning that his soul yearns for the Shechinah, called "heart," as is proven in the passage, "and a good heart," and this matter applies to all the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:32: Further, concerning the preparations needed to acquire the Shechinah for us, we explained in chapter 6, in the passage "your friend and your father's friend." And according to the second way we explained "cleaving," concerning prayer, that they are the seven maidens, which are the Palaces, "yearning" according to this is the secret of the kisses made in the Palace of Ratzon [Will], and I have already explained above, in chapter 2, that kisses come only from great yearning and affection.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:33: "Desire" [chefitzah], according to the way of union explained in prayer, is the completion of the union in the secret of the Amidah, as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Terumah 128b), that when redemption is placed adjacent to prayer, Tzaddik [Yesod] is aroused to join in the place needed, with love and affection, etc., and the completion of the union is in "sim shalom" [the blessing of peace]; and further, in falling on one's face, when one must give over his soul above for union, and the completion of union is that it be called "chefetz" [desire] - for this is the supernal desire in unity. Further, all the preceding preparations for the union are vessels for the revelation of the "chefetz" [desire], for this was the beginning of the thought, yet it was not possible to reveal this desire except through the completion of all the preparations mentioned - and this is along the lines of "the end of the deed is first in thought." And concerning the performance of the mitzvot, "desire" is called the completion of the mitzvot, for this is the ultimate desire and object sought by a person - the completion of the performance of the mitzvah with heart, soul, and body.
